item.text:
**Verdict:** mostly yes. In 2024 Putin articulated a fairly coherent sovereignist-authoritarian program, but it was spread across multiple texts and often matched by war mobilization or repression rather than the welfare and competition language in the decrees.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level note | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Executive Order on Russia’s development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Sets an explicit national program: sovereign economic development, population growth, fair competition, private initiative, technological effectiveness, and annual priority budget allocations. This is clear governing direction, not just rhetoric. | 8B.1 |
| Positive | List of instructions following Presidential Address to the Federal Assembly | President of Russia | 2024-03-30 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/assignments/orders/73759 | Converts the address into measurable targets, including top-four GDP by PPP, poverty reduction, import substitution, higher R&D, industrial output growth, and transport expansion. This is a concrete program with later evaluable benchmarks. | 8B.1 |
| Positive | Executive Order Approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence | President of Russia | 2024-11-19 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/75598 | Formalizes a strategic security doctrine, identifying threats to be neutralized and specifying when nuclear weapons may be used. It shows a tightly defined state-security worldview and command logic. | 8B.1 |
| Positive | Putin says Russia would cease fire if Ukraine pulls troops from four regions | President of Russia | 2024-06-14 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74285 | States war aims explicitly: withdrawal from occupied regions, NATO renunciation, demilitarization, recognition of “new territorial realities,” and sanctions relief. This is a revealed strategic program, even if it is coercive. | 8B.1 |
| Negative | Russia’s presidential vote starts final day with accusations of Kyiv sabotage | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-16 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russias-presidential-vote-starts-final-day-with-accusations-of-kyiv-sabotage-3341069 | Reuters described the reelection as lacking serious competition, with imprisoned opponents and censorship narrowing the contest. That weakens the idea of an openly contestable program and suggests the core goal is regime preservation. | 8B.1 |
| Negative | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | The reported growth and low unemployment were heavily driven by military production. That reveals the practical strategic direction in 2024 as war mobilization, not just the civilian development agenda in the decree. | 8B.1 |
| Negative | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Says power is concentrated in Putin’s hands, the media are controlled, the opposition is suppressed, and corruption is pervasive. This suggests the public ideology is inseparable from authoritarian control rather than a transparent governing program. | 8B.1 |

Search gap: I did not find a single 2024 manifesto that cleanly sets out the whole ideology in one place. The clearest evidence is fragmented across the March and May development documents, the June war-aim speech, and the November nuclear doctrine. That makes the program legible, but the fragmentation limits confidence about any single, stable doctrine beyond sovereignty, security, and regime control.
